prompt_en: Photorealistic candid street photograph at a rain-soaked bus stop late at night. One stranded commuter, clearly an adult, is the only person left at the stop, caught in the missed-last-bus moment as the last bus is already pulling away from the curb in the same frame. The bus’s closed rear doors, receding tail lamps, and narrow spray behind its wheels make departure unmistakable; a small illuminated timetable on the shelter marks this as the final service. Keep the adult in the near left third and the receding bus in the far right third; the empty boarding space between them makes the missed connection readable as the scene recedes into wet darkness. The commuter stands with both feet planted on the pavement just behind the curb, right hand gripping a bundle of wet documents at waist height; rain has softened their corners and streaked the ink. Their left arm hangs slack, shoulders fold inward, and the commuter’s face shows deflated disappointment as their eyes follow the bus. The grip, sodden pages, and face remain unobstructed. A cold shelter tube grazes the wet face and papers while the bus’s red rear lamps stain the puddles between the adult and the vehicle. A passing pedestrian’s hurried photograph sets a slightly off-level, human-height viewpoint, as though a phone was lifted for one quick shot while walking by. Hold both the stranded adult and the departing bus legibly in one frame, with rain-wet reflections and imperfect motion blur at the edges, natural street lighting, and ordinary, unstaged clothing.
